2.problem: Define a sequence of polynomials recursively by \(P_1(x) = 2x^2 - 1\) and \(P_n(x) = P_{n-1}\left(P_{n-1}(x)\right)\) for \(n \ge 2\). How many distinct real roots of \(P_4\) lie between \(-\frac{1}{2}\) and \(\frac{1}{2}\), inclusive?
2.solutions:
Note that \(P_1(\cos\theta) = 2\cos^2\theta - 1 = \cos(2\theta)\). We claim that \(P_n(\cos\theta) = \cos\left(2^{2^{n-1}}\theta\right)\).

The base case is given above. For the inductive step, note that \[P_{n+1}(\cos\theta) = P_n\left(P_n(\cos\theta)\right) = P_n\left(\cos\left(2^{2^{n-1}}\theta\right)\right) = \cos\left(2^{2^{n-1}} \cdot 2^{2^{n-1}}\theta\right) = \cos\left(2^{2^n}\theta\right).\]

In particular, we have \(P_4(\cos\theta) = \cos(256\theta)\). Thus we have that \(\cos\left(\frac{(2k+1)\pi}{512}\right)\) are distinct roots of \(P_4\) for \(k = 0, 1, \ldots, 255\). Since \(P_4\) has degree \(256\), these are all the roots of \(P_4\). Thus it suffices to find the number of \(k\) such that \[\frac{\pi}{3} \le \frac{(2k+1)\pi}{512} \le \frac{2\pi}{3},\] or equivalently, \[512 \le 6k + 3 \le 1024.\] There are exactly \(\boxed{86}\) such \(k\).
